subject: ApexMart service surge readout & corrective action plan
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@apexmart.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Grey <tom.grey@apexmart.com>, noc@apexmart.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency & 5xx spike hitting checkout — immediate readout requested

Team,

This morning between ~07:50–08:30 PDT we saw a sustained latency spike (p50 -> 1.2s, p95 -> 6.3s) and a sharp increase in 5xx errors tied to the Redwood integration on Checkout v2. Impact: ~18% of checkout requests failed or timed out; revenue path impaired. Our SREs opened a bridge and we traced the pattern to repeated tokenization/response retries — we believe it's on the Redwood side but need confirmation.

We need: an executive readout today (summary + RCA), a short-term mitigation plan we can expect within 24 hours, and a proposal for SLO credits. Please confirm ownership, timeline, and next steps. This is causing customer complaints; legal and ops are watching.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Engineering, ApexMart
(415) 555-0134

Attachment: apex_incident_kpi_snapshot.csv (summary of affected transactions)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@apexmart.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency & 5xx spike hitting checkout — immediate readout requested

Sarah — thanks for the flag and the data. We're on this.

Immediate actions:
- I've opened an incident bridge and assigned Marcus and Karthik to lead triage.
- We are collecting request traces and prefix cache metrics; expecting initial RCA hypothesis within 3 hours.
- I'll send an executive summary and contingency timeline within 4 hours, and a full corrective plan by EOB PST.

Short ask for you: can you share the top 10 example request IDs from the CSV (or paste two examples) so we can prioritize logs?

I'll stay on the bridge and keep you updated.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: ApexMart — bridge notes & action owner assignment

Team — quick internal notes from the bridge:
- Symptoms: sustained p95 latency regression, 5xx spike clustered on model shards serving Checkout v2. No deploys in customer region at the time.
- Initial signals: KV cache churn and repeated cache misses causing request hot-path amplification + a problematic kernel fallback on older GPU instances.
- Business impact: ~18% checkout failures for ApexMart high-value users. Exec visibility likely.

Action owners:
- Marcus: produce RCA (kernel selection + cache churn root cause), rapid mitigation (patch or rolling restart plan). Due: 3 hours. Attach initial log extract.
- Karthik: craft canary rollback / routing rule to shift traffic to a stable model variant, coordinate with infra and Dedicated teams. Due: 2 hours.
- Kimberly: draft customer-facing exec summary and SLO credit position; coordinate legal if needed. Due: 3 hours.

Attachments: apex_incident_kpi_snapshot.csv (from Apex), I'll attach our initial trace extraction once processed.

Stephanie

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: ApexMart — bridge notes & action owner assignment

Summary RCA and immediate corrective measures (high level):

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by traces):
- Under high concurrent checkout load, the runtime switched to a fallback kernel path for a subset of tokens when KV cache lookups returned unexpected shapes. This triggered additional per-request tokenization passes and repeated retry attempts; those retries amplified queueing and produced 5xx from the model worker under memory pressure.

Immediate mitigations (next 24h):
1) Traffic steering: apply routing rule to shift 60% of ApexMart traffic to a retained stable variant (model-v1.4-quant) — reduces exposure immediately. (Owner: Karthik)
2) Restart plan: rolling restart of 12 affected GPU workers with a patched kernel selection flag. Rolling restart to run in 3-4 waves, target completion 12 hours. (Owner: Marcus)
3) Hotfix: backport kernel selector guard to prevent fallback path on cache shape mismatch; deploy as hotfix to canary group tonight after verification. (Owner: Marcus/Karthik)
4) Customer comms: executive readout + SLO credit proposal (Kimberly). Draft attached.

Notes: attached a diff for the kernel guard (playbook_patch.diff) and a preliminary corrective_actions_v1.pdf with timelines. I recommend we schedule a 30-min exec readout at 15:00 PDT and invite Apex execs.

Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@apexmart.com>, Tom Grey <tom.grey@apexmart.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: ApexMart executive readout + confirmed corrective actions and credits

Sarah / Tom — thank you for your patience while we investigated. Executive summary below and a short list of concrete commitments.

What happened (one-sentence): a fallback kernel path under specific KV cache-shape mismatch conditions caused repeated tokenization/retry behavior that amplified latency and led to memory pressure on a subset of GPU workers, resulting in elevated p95 and a transient 5xx spike.

What we did:
- Immediately shifted 60% of traffic to a stable model variant to stop the amplification.
- Performed a controlled rolling restart of the affected worker pool (completed within 12 hours).
- Deployed a kernel-selector guard hotfix to prevent the fallback path during cache shape mismatches.
- Added additional request-level observability (trace tags) and guardrails to detect recurrence.

Customer commitments & timeline:
- Short-term: we completed mitigation and restored normal error rates; full metrics validation completed 24h after rollout (complete).
- Mid-term (2 weeks): release a runtime patch improving cache-shape validation and reduce miss-rate; automated canary for kernel selector.
- Compensation: proposed SLO credit equal to 10% of April billed usage for affected routes — legal is prepared to finalize. (attachment: corrective_actions_v1.pdf)

Requested confirmation: please acknowledge receipt and confirm whether the proposed credit and the 30-day follow-up validation plan are acceptable. We will schedule a joint post-incident review to walk the technical team through the mitigations and timeline.

Thanks — we will keep a dedicated channel open for any residual concerns.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachment: corrective_actions_v1.pdf
